newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai property loan problems said under control.
newsitem.headline: Thai property loan problems said under control.

text.p: Problems relating to property loans given by Thai financial institutions are not at a worrisome level and the Bank of Thailand is monitoring the situation closely, a central bank official said on Thursday.

"Property loan problems are under control. We (BOT) are closely monitoring (the problem)," Nongnart Sondysuwan, deputy director of the BOT's Financial Institutions Supervision and Development Department, told Reuters.

Thai stocks have tumbled to their lowest in over three years now on the back of sustained selling in recent weeks by foreign and local investors after rumours abounded about cash flow problems said to be faced by property firms.
Investors have sold off property in recent weeks as developers face a hard time raising domestic loans amid a glut in residential and business unit in Bangkok, brokers said.

The property sector has also been hurt by news that the president of Somprasong Land Plc, Prasong Panichpakdi, Is facing charges of falsifying company financial statement. He turned himself in to police for questioning on Thursday.
Investors have also been disposing of bank and finance stocks on worries that some of the financial institutions may face defaults on property loans which would impact earnings, analysts said.
A large portion of banks' lending portfolios are said by analysts to be granted to property companies.

The BOT's Nongnart said the loans granted by domestic financial institutions to unproductive and speculative property projects had slowed this year and were in line with the central bank's guidelines.

"The central bank had attempted to trim down loans for golf course development, luxury condominiums and the purchase of undeveloped lands. The proportion of the loans to these unproductive projects has declined," she said without giving figures.

According to BOT data, cumulative outstanding loans granted by banks and finance companies to the property sector at the end of August amounted to 753.09 billion baht ($30.12 billion), representing 13.96 percent of their total lending.
This compared with outstanding loans to the property sector totalling 710.79 billion baht or 14.96 percent of all bank and finance company lending at the end of 1995.
"The loans to property sector had been slowing as the central bank wants all financial institutions to be careful in lending to new property projects," Nongnart said.
She added that the BOT would not ease tight measures on lending to the property sector by local financial institutions despite a slump in the sector.
"We understand the situation of the property sector right now. But the measures were aimed at maintaining the stability of the economy in the long term," she said.
